title: Three AI Coders. One Broken App.
script: I gave three AI coders the same broken app. Five bugs. One clean starting point. Login fails. Search ignores capitals. Mobile navigation overflows. Save does nothing. One test is already red. Each gets the identical prompt, the same limit, and no help from me unless I log it. Here is the important part: a confident summary does not count as a fix. The app has to pass the checks. The verified result was [FIXES_A], [FIXES_B], and [FIXES_C] fixes. [REGRESSION_SUMMARY]. [EVIDENCE_BASED_WINNER_OR_TIE]. Which agent should face the harder test next?
timingStatus: Estimated silent editorial timings. Refit scenes and caption timestamps to the unchanged voice-over when supplied.
concept: Five deliberate bugs; identical repo/prompt; compare fixes, runtime and regressions.
whyNow: AI coding and automation promises are judged by a reproducible useful task.
viewerGoal: Understand what the system actually completed and where supervision matters.
hooks: I gave three AI coders the same broken app. Five bugs. One clean starting point.
Five broken features. Three confident AI coders.
Which AI actually fixes the app, not just the summary?
strongestHook: I gave three AI coders the same broken app. Five bugs. One clean starting point.
directorBrief: Direct this as an observable challenge: Five deliberate bugs; identical repo/prompt; compare fixes, runtime and regressions. The viewer must see the starting problem, the exact constraint, one revealing action and the independently checked output. Let the real failure or correction create the turn. Save every first attempt. Completion claims alone never establish a result.
effort: 15–60 minutes core build/test; allow additional audit/edit time.
protocol: Prepare one local React fixture with five independently reproducible faults: invalid login handling, case-sensitive search, navigation overflow at 639px, dead Save action, and a seeded failing unit test. Freeze baseline commit, dependency versions and five acceptance checks. Select three accessible coding tools; record their exact model/configuration. Run one identical prompt on separate clean copies with a 20-minute cap and identical resource access. Log interventions, submission-to-verified-finish time, five fixes and regressions. No winner unless checks establish it; one run is exploratory, repeat before a broad claim.
evidenceRequirements: Run each tool on an identical clean copy; fill the scoreboard only from actual tests.
thumbnailDirection: Use the opening object or strongest real evidence crop. Put “Three Coders Five Bugs” in the top-middle safe area; one accent, no extra subheading.
ending: [EVIDENCE_BASED_WINNER_OR_TIE]. Which agent should face the harder test next?
instagramCaption: Three AI Coders. One Broken App.. Five deliberate bugs; identical repo/prompt; compare fixes, runtime and regressions. Full test conditions and limitations belong beside the final result. [EVIDENCE_BASED_WINNER_OR_TIE]. Which agent should face the harder test next?
tiktokCaption: Three AI Coders. One Broken App.. WHO GETS ROUND TWO?
music: Original/licensed light percussive electronic bed, 100–115 BPM; leave real clicks readable. No music asset is included.
recordings: Full continuous source run plus selected genuine action clips. Record 1080p or higher, readable UI, cursor, exact OS/tool/plan and run clock. Keep uncropped originals.
screenshots: Baseline, first attempt, final output, official license/plan/version, and each verdict evidence frame. Synthetic fixtures only.
icons: Use original vector shapes and existing studio-kit Icon components; use official product marks only for identification. No random decorative icon grid.
assetBrief: Broken/final app, three runs, identical prompt, test output.
